The petitioners, who were appointed as Designated Officers under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 in the Department of Food Safety and Drugs Administration, were repatriated to the Public Health Department and posted as Assistant Surgeons.

sentences.text: The reliving orders and the c o n s e q u e n t i a l t r a n s f e r o r d e r s a r e c h a l l e n g e d i n t h e s e w r i t p e t i t i o n s .

( Uploaded on: 19/05/2025 10:28:19 am ) WP(MD)Nos.14930 of 2017 and 14128 of 2019 2.Since the issue involved in both writ petitions is similar, the writ petitions are taken up together and disposed of by this common order.

3.All these petitioners have been appointed as Assistant Surgeons in the Tamil Nadu Medical Services and they were working as Medical Officers in the Primary Health Centres under the control of the Director of Public Health and Preventive Medicines.
The Central Government has enacted the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and it was implemented all over India with effect from 05.08.2011.

The provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 [herein shall be referred to as the Act] mandate the appointment of Designated Officers under Section 36 of the Act to implement the provisions of the Act in district level.
The petitioners were appointed as Designated Officers in the year 2011 and as such they have been serving as Designated Officers.
While so, by the impugned orders, they have been relieved, transferred and posted in the Primary Health Centres in the Tamil Nadu Medical Services.

4.The learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners were appointed as Designated Officers in the year 2011 and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 19/05/2025 10:28:19 am ) WP(MD)Nos.14930 of 2017 and 14128 of 2019 2012 in the Department of Food Safety and Drugs Administration and they have been duly working for more than 10 years.

entities.text: Department of Food Safety and Drugs Administration
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: They have been permanently relieved from the post of Assistant Surgeons from the Tamil Nadu Medical Services and they have been paid salary from the Food Safety Department.
Therefore they have been made as permanent employees of the Food Safety Department.
While so, without any reasons, they have been reverted to their parent department that their performances in implementing the Act in the district are not satisfactory.

This according to the learned Counsel for the petitioners is in violation of the service conditions of the petitioners, without following the principle of natural justice and the impugned orders are stigmatic one.
5.The learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the respondents 1 to 3 submits that the petitioners as well as others from the Department of Public Health and Preventive Medicines were deputed and appointed on temporary basis in the 2nd respondent department as Designated C.Suresh Babu vs The State Of Tamil Nadu on 16 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54769550/

The petitioners / Medical Officers were https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

The new post of Designated Officers were established for a period of one year with further continuance to be made from time to time.
They have not been observed permanently.
The service rules have not been framed yet.
However, a lien and seniority of these Designated Officers are preserved and maintained in their parent department.

Therefore,
according to the learned Additional Advocate General, due to the urgent implementation of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the Medical Officers / Health Officers from Public Health and Preventive Medicines Department were appointed as Designated Officers on temporary basis.

sentences.text: As per Section 36 of the Act, the Commissioner of Food Safety shall by notification appoint Designated Officers for the purpose of performing the functions under the Act and the petitioners were appointed only on deputation and now they have been repatriated to the parent department.
The petitioners who were appointed on temporary basis cannot claim preferential right.
Their lien and seniority is still maintained in their parent department.

6.This Court considered the rival submissions made and perused the materials placed on record.

7.The Government of India consolidated the laws relating to the food and has brought in an integrated food law namely, the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, notified on 24.08.2006.
8.The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 repealed the Tamil Nadu Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 was implemented in Tamil Nadu with effect from 05.08.2011.
Section 36 of the Act mandates appointment of Designated Offices for each district.
They are in-charge of the food safety administration in the districts, issuance and cancellation of license for the business operators, etc.,

While implementing the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, in the year 2011 on temporary basis the Medical Officers, who were working in the Health Department and Primary Health Centres were deputed to the Food Safety and Drugs Administration Department on temporary basis with effect from 05.08.2011 by the Commissioner of Food Safety and Drugs https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

9.The lien and seniority of these Designated Officers is preserved and maintained in their parent department.

It has been reiterated by the Commissioner of Food Safety and Drugs Department to the Director of Public Health and Preventive Medicines and Health and Family Welfare Department in R.No.2413/12/S2/FSSA, dated 01.10.2012 and the same is extracted as under:

Till then the lien and seniority of these Food Safety Officers drawn from the cadre of former Health Inspectors / Sanitary Inspectors etc., with training as Food Inspector under the repealed preventive of Food Adulteration have to be preserved and maintained with resultant benefits to them in their parent department.

10.The Secretary to the Government, Food Safety and Drugs Administration Department in letter No.25336/M1/2015-3 dated 29.07.2015 has also clarified that till date no one has been absorbed by the Commissioner of Food Safety and Drug Administration from their parent Department.
11.The respondents claim that 12 Designated Officers were already relieved to their parent department of Public Health and Preventive Medicines and they have been appointed in their original post.
It appears that the petitioners have also joined in their parent department, pursuant to the impugned orders.

This Court in WP(MD)No.14930 of 2017 on 12.09.2024 has passed an order as under:
7.On
a prima facie consideration

, this Court is of the considered view that once the respective petitioners https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 19/05/2025 10:28:19 am ) WP(MD)Nos.14930 of 2017 and 14128 of 2019 have joined duty in their parent department, as per the impugned order, by giving letters to the Deputy Director of Health Services, Cheyyar, Stating that they are willing to join duty as per the impugned order at the Government Primary Health Centre, S.V.Nagaram and the Government Primary Health Centre, Peranamalur, respectively and the contempt petition having already been closed after recording the said fact, the question of re-adjudicating the issue at this stage may not arise.

12.The qualifications for the Designated Officers are prescribed under Rule No.
2.1.2.1 of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011 as under:
2.1.2: Designated Officer 1. Qualification - (i) The Designated Officer shall be a whole time Officer, not below the rank of Sub-Divisional Officer or equivalent and shall possess a Bachelors or Masters or Doctorate degree in Science with chemistry as one of the subjects or shall possesses at least one of the educational qualifications prescribed for the Food Safety Officers C.Suresh Babu vs The State Of Tamil Nadu on 16 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54769550/
6 under these rules or who has possessing not less than five years of experience as Food Safety Officers or has not less than seven years combined experience as Food Safety https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 19/05/2025 10:28:19 am )
WP(MD)Nos.14930 of 2017 and 14128 of 2019 Officer and Food Inspector of which minimum four years as Food Safety Officer after commencement of the Food Safety and Standards Act:
Provided that the Commissioner of Food Safety may with the previous approval of the State Government, confer a Sub-Divisional Officer of the area, additional charge as Designated Officer for same period as may be specified by the Food Authority.
Provided further that the Chief Executive Officer may confer any officer of the Central Government with additional charge as Designated Officer for the area outside the jurisdiction of State Government or Union territory Government]
(ii) He shall Undergo training as may be specified by the Food Authority, within a period of six months from the date of his appointment as Designated Officer.
(iii) (a) persons having been appointed as food Inspector having qualification prescribed under the PFA Rules, 1955 or as Local Health Authority [or appointed as Food Safety Officer having qualification prescribed under these rules] shall be eligible for appointment as Designated Officer, subject to fulfilling such other conditions as may be prescribed for the post of Designated Officer by the State Government.

13.The
petitioners were appointed on temporary basis as Designated Officers on deputation and they have been allowed to continue for several years.
The services rules have not been framed yet for these Designated Officers.
The Commissioner of Food Safety claims that the Government has taken expeditious steps to frame ad-hoc rules for the Designated Officers and it will be finalised within five months.
Therefore, admittedly there is no service rules.
The petitioners were appointed only on temporary basis at the time of urgent implementation of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

sentences.text: 22. As per the Rules, the qualification for being appointed as Designated Officers is satisfied if the applicant has obtained a Degree in Science with Chemistry as a subject.

Thus, we can safely conclude that the functions of a Designated Officers can be discharged even by a person who is merely a holder of a Bachelor Degree in Science with Chemistry as one of the subject.
But, on the other hand, the petitioners who are all Professional Doctors, are alone capable of meeting 26 the requirements of the Health and Family Welfare Services Department.

entities.text: Health and Family Welfare Services Department
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hence, the decision of the State Government has to be appreciated in acting wisely to withdraw the services of the petitioners who are deputed to Executive Post and deploying them in the appropriate posts where they would be able to better utilize their professional skills to serve the society in an appropriate manner.
23. It is obvious that the petitioners have orchestrated this litigation only with an intention of retaining the posts of the Designated Officers.
It is bemusing and befuddling as to why professionals like the petitioners are yearning to covet the posts of Designated Officers.

The petitioners who have all acquired the licence to save human lives by their dint of sheer hard work are coveting the posts of a designated officer whose educational requirement is only a Bachelor degree in Science with Chemistry as https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 19/05/2025 10:28:19 am ) WP(MD)Nos.14930 of 2017 and 14128 of 2019 a subject.
Even by their own 27 pleadings the petitioners have admitted that they have been asked to hand over charge to officials from the Group C cadres.

Even though it is settled law that an Officer on deputation has no lien or right to the Office where he is deputed, the petitioners have orchestrated this litigation and resisted the attempt of State Government to rectify their earlier mistake committed under the notification dated 13.01.2014.

The resistance to the repatriation is wholly unjustified and accordingly,
rejected by the Tribunal.
This Court deems fit and necessary to deprecate the conduct of the petitioners.

24. The attempts by the petitioners to evade and avoid repatriation to the parent department to discharge the duties for which they were originally selected is tantamount to lack of devotion to duty and though this Court deems fit and proper to visit the petitioners with heavy costs the same is not levied keeping in mind their stature as doctors and that they have subsequently 28 taken charge in places where they have been transferred.
15.This
Court has also passed similar order dated 05.02.2018 in W.P.No.2438 of 2018 and order dated 06.08.2018 in W.P.No.540 of 2017.

The petitioners, who were appointed as Designated Officers on temporary basis cannot claim as a matter of right to continue in the same post, when lien C.Suresh Babu vs The State Of Tamil Nadu on 16 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54769550/
8 and seniority is preserved and maintained with benefits in their parent department.

Accordingly these writ petitions are dismissed.

16.The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been enacted to ensure a systematic and scientific development of food processing industries and to ensure that manufacturing, import, processing,
distribution and sale of food are in compliance with the food laws.
The role of the Designated Officers and the Food Safety Officers are very crucial in implementing the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

The temporary arrangement made at the time of implementation of the Act in the year 2011 has been allowed to continue for several years and the Government has not yet framed ad-hoc rules for the implementation of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

17.The Officers without the qualifications prescribed in the Rules are allowed to continue for several years and therefore, the very implementation of the Food Safety and Standards Act in the State is not effective.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

19.The Government has to take necessary initiative to make necessary rules for effective implementation of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
20. Section 86 of the Food Safety and Standards Act empowers the Central Government to issue necessary directions to the State Government for carrying out all or any of the provisions of the Act.

In the event of any failure on the part of the State Government, the newly impleaded respondent /
the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India shall issue necessary instructions as provided under Section 86 of the Act, to the State Government to ensure effective implementation of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 in the State.

opennyai_summary.facts: The Central Government has enacted the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and it was implemented all over India with effect from 05.08.2011.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
petitioners were appointed on temporary basis as Designated Officers on deputation and they have been allowed to continue for several years.
The services rules have not been framed yet for these Designated Officers.
Therefore, admittedly there is no service rules.
The petitioners were appointed only on temporary basis at the time of urgent implementation of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
22. As per the Rules, the qualification for being appointed as Designated Officers is satisfied if the applicant has obtained a Degree in Science with Chemistry as a subject.
Thus, we can safely conclude that the functions of a Designated Officers can be discharged even by a person who is merely a holder of a Bachelor Degree in Science with Chemistry as one of the subject.
But, on the other hand, the petitioners who are all Professional Doctors, are alone capable of meeting 26 the requirements of the Health and Family Welfare Services Department.
Hence, the decision of the State Government has to be appreciated in acting wisely to withdraw the services of the petitioners who are deputed to Executive Post and deploying them in the appropriate posts where they would be able to better utilize their professional skills to serve the society in an appropriate manner.
It is bemusing and befuddling as to why professionals like the petitioners are yearning to covet the posts of Designated Officers.
Even though it is settled law that an Officer on deputation has no lien or right to the Office where he is deputed, the petitioners have orchestrated this litigation and resisted the attempt of State Government to rectify their earlier mistake committed under the notification dated 13.01.2014.
The resistance to the repatriation is wholly unjustified and accordingly,
rejected by the Tribunal.
